auditor.mutationScope: Only this audit JSON was written; source, runtime, evidence, manifests and prior audits were not edited.

evidenceLimits.method: CPU triangle projection of actual Three.js geometry with approximated material fills
canProve: silhouette, placement, occlusion and phone-scale readability
cannotProve: bloom, post-processing or live HDR lighting
evidenceLimits.separation: White glint strips prove authored highlight geometry but not delicious PBR response. Failure at 090/180 and repeated large silhouettes are geometry or placement faults, not CPU-material limitations.

comparison.finding: Cleared the disk-fountain family with one thick cliff sheet, but the isolated close floated in a blue void and did not prove its cliff lip, source reservoir or receiving pool.
Added a rigid upper ledge/cap to the close, improving upstream contact, but the curtain still floated without a terrain wall or downstream pool.

The close now includes a real cliff slab, dark rock recess, broad sheet/ropes, highlight streaks and a receiving pool. Terrain binding and continuity are materially improved; orbit visibility is essentially unchanged from r23.

viewScores.finding: The mission is visible as a thick orange front-right body, but palace and Pollinator Yard still compete with it and the cliff attachment is not the first read.
Best world view: the sheet crosses the ledge and descends with actual width and depth. It still resembles a trunk/root mass more than a broad sparkling waterfall.
The Great Honeyfall is largely occluded; only a cap/fragment remains and the terrain-to-pool chain cannot be parsed.
The mission disappears as a named feature. Rear palace authorship remains good, but no Honeyfall system is readable.
Several orange ropes persist behind the Pollinator Yard, proving volume but not one coherent cliff-to-pool event.
The opposite front oblique restores the attached curtain and broad lower honey mass. The top disk and repeated ropes remain visually simple.
Clay confirms the overall world is true 360 but cannot isolate the front-side mission from the rear.

R27's decisive gain: a thick sheet overlaps an actual cliff slab, descends in fused ropes past dark rock and lands in a visible pool. It no longer floats. The flat plank lip, repeated rear lobes, parallel rope ends and circular pool rim still keep it below source-quality liquid sculpture.
The orange curtain survives at phone scale but remains secondary; large underside columns and sparse atmospheric bowls dominate the world read.

cleared.evidence: The r27 close includes an overlapping cliff wall and receiving pool.
The curtain has real side thickness and changes coherently across favorable obliques.

active.evidence: The mission is not readable at 090 or 180 and remains ambiguous at 270.
CPU glint polygons cannot prove refraction, clearcoat, reflections, attenuation or stable transparent overlap.

rankedFixes.fix: Add authored side and rear terrain-fed spill faces or secondary cliff cascades so 090, 180 and 270 preserve reservoir-to-fall-to-pool identity without duplicating a front card.
Replace the rigid horizontal lip and three bulbous cap lobes with an irregular rock reservoir/meniscus that visibly feeds the broad sheet.
Merge parallel lower ropes into asymmetrical sheets, fused drips, impact bulges and a non-circular pooled overflow; remove repeated rear sphere lobes.
Capture a live WebGL fixed-orbit and close proof showing transmission, attenuation, environment reflections, clearcoat glints and stable transparency sorting.
Reduce repeated underside columns and replace distant bowl islets with authored hive silhouettes and real haze so the Honeyfall remains a focal event at phone scale.

overall.familyDisposition: retain r27 terrain-bound close and cliff-sheet family; continue only with orbit-coverage and live-material proof
overall.summary: R27 is the best Honeyfall revision so far and clears the floating-curtain veto. It is terrain-bound, moderately gooey and carries authored glint geometry in close proof. It is not visible as a Great Honeyfall around the full orbit, and the CPU packet cannot approve the requested delicious PBR material response.
